message.content:
The email arrived on a Tuesday, predictably. Subject line: "Northwood High - 20 Year Reunion - Volunteers Needed!" Noel almost deleted it without a second glance. Twenty years. An eternity, really. He hadn't thought about Northwood in… well, he hadn’t thought about it much at all. It existed as a faded photograph in the album of his past, a sepia-toned memory of awkward dances and questionable fashion choices. 

He hesitated, the cursor hovering over the delete button. It wasn't nostalgia pulling him up short. It was something else, a faint stirring of… what? Curiosity? Perhaps a morbid fascination with revisiting a place he'd actively tried to forget. He clicked the email open. The tone was relentlessly cheerful, all exclamation points and promises of a "fantastic evening of reminiscing and reconnecting." A committee, apparently, had been formed, and they were desperately seeking volunteers to help with everything from securing a venue to compiling a list of attendees.

Noel scrolled through the bullet points, scanning for anything remotely appealing. “Decorations Coordinator,” “Music Selection Committee,” “Photo Archive Digitization.” It was all so… intensely ordinary. And yet, something about the sheer, unadulterated effort being put into this reunion struck him as oddly compelling. It felt like a determined act of defiance against the inevitable march of time, a desperate grasp at a moment that had already slipped away.

He surprised himself by replying. “I’m willing to help with the attendee list,” he typed, then immediately regretted it. Why on earth had he done that? He wasn’t sure he even *wanted* to see a list of people from Northwood, let alone be responsible for compiling one. He hit send anyway, a sudden impulse overriding his better judgment. 

The response came almost instantly. “Fantastic! Welcome aboard, Noel! We’ll be in touch shortly with details about our first meeting. Best, Eleanor Vance – Reunion Coordinator.” Eleanor Vance. The name registered with a strange familiarity. He vaguely remembered her, a teacher, perhaps? English, maybe? 

He tried to place her face, but it remained stubbornly elusive, a blurry image at the edge of his memory. He quickly dismissed it as insignificant, a trick of the light. He had a life now, a perfectly good life in a different city, with different people. Why was he letting a high school reunion dredge up all these unnecessary questions?

The meeting was scheduled for Saturday morning at the local library. Noel marked it on his calendar, a small knot of apprehension tightening in his stomach. He told himself it was just nerves, the anxiety of facing a room full of strangers, people he hadn’t seen in two decades. But deep down, a tiny voice whispered that it was something more, something he couldn’t quite name. He glanced at the calendar again, the date looming like a silent question mark.
